summaryEn: Musk hosts the investor conference call laying out the rationale for Tesla's proposed acquisition of SolarCity and his vision of a single integrated sustainable-energy company.
summaryZh: 马斯克主持投资者电话会议，阐述 Tesla 拟议收购 SolarCity 的理由，以及他对一家统一整合的可持续能源公司的愿景。

segments.textEn: Good day, ladies and gentlemen, welcome to the Tesla Motors conference call. At this time, all participants are in
segments.textZh: 大家好，女士们、先生们，欢迎参加 Tesla Motors 电话会议。此时，所有与会者均处于

segments.textEn: a listen only mode.
segments.textZh: 仅收听模式。

segments.textEn: Later we will conduct the question and answer session and instructions will follow at that time. If anyone should require assistance during the call, please press Star then zero on your touchtone telephone. As a reminder, this conference may be recorded. I would like to introduce your host for today's conference, Mr. Jeff Evanson, Investor Relations, Tesla Motors.
segments.textZh: 稍后我们将进行问答环节，届时会提供相关操作说明。如果有人在电话会议期间需要协助，请在按键式电话上先按星号键，再按0。提醒一下，本次会议可能会被录音。现在请允许我介绍今天会议的主持人，Tesla Motors 投资者关系负责人 Jeff Evanson 先生。

segments.textEn: So you may begin.

segments.textEn: Thank you Terea and good morning everyone. Welcome to Tesla's call to discuss the rationale for our offer to acquire SolarCity. I'm joined today by Elon Musk, Tesla Chairman and CEO Todd Marin, Tesla General Counsel J.B. strabo, our CTO and CFO Jason Wheeler. Yesterday we announced our offer to acquire SolarCity in filings with the SEC and through a blog post available at www.tes.
segments.textZh: 谢谢你，Terea，大家早上好。欢迎参加 Tesla 的电话会议，讨论我们收购 SolarCity 的要约所依据的理由。今天与我一同出席的有 Tesla 董事长兼首席执行官埃隆·马斯克、Tesla 总法律顾问 Todd Marin、我们的首席技术官 J.B. strabo，以及首席财务官 Jason Wheeler。昨天，我们通过提交给美国证券交易委员会的文件宣布了收购 SolarCity 的要约，并发布了一篇可在 www.tes. 查阅的博客文章。

Actual events or results could differ materially due to a number of risks and uncertainties, including those mentioned in our most recent Form 10Q filed with the SEC.
segments.textZh: 在今天上午的电话会议期间，我们将讨论部分业务展望，并作出其他前瞻性陈述。这些陈述基于我们截至今天的预测和预期。由于多项风险和不确定性，包括我们最近向美国证券交易委员会提交的10-Q表格中提到的风险和不确定性，实际事件或结果可能存在重大差异。

segments.speakerZh: 杰夫·埃文森（投资者关系）

segments.textEn: Good morning everyone. Thanks, Jeff.
segments.textZh: 大家早上好。谢谢，Jeff。

segments.textEn: So I just wanted to briefly touch
segments.textZh: 所以我只是想简要谈谈

segments.textEn: on some of the process points and
segments.textZh: 一些流程方面的要点，以及

segments.textEn: why yesterday's announcement might have looked somewhat different to people who normally see these kinds of announcements. It's actually somewhat of an easy explanation, but it is somewhat of a unique situation. So usually I know that everyone is used to seeing an announcement when there is actually a definitive agreement that is reached and not just simply an offer. And obviously in our situation, we were only announcing an offer and then as a result, you didn't receive the same kind of information that you would receive when an agreement is reached, such as the agreement itself and detailed financial information about the combined company.
segments.textZh: 为什么昨天的公告在通常看到这类公告的人看来可能有些不同。其实解释起来比较容易，但这确实是一种有些独特的情况。所以通常，我知道大家习惯于在确实达成最终协议时看到公告，而不是只有一项要约。显然，在我们的情形中，我们宣布的只是一项要约，因此，你们没有收到达成协议时会收到的同类信息，例如协议本身以及有关合并后公司的详细财务信息。

segments.textEn: The reason for that is that Elon is a 5% stockholder in SolarCity and he's required by the securities laws to keep the market informed through a Schedule 13D filing about his plans with respect to those holdings. And because of Tesla's decision to make an offer to SolarCity and Elon's support for that decision, it was appropriate to amend his schedule 13D to update the market even though no definitive agreement had yet been reached.
segments.textZh: 原因是，埃隆是SolarCity持股5%的股东，证券法要求他通过提交附表13D，让市场及时了解他对于这些持股的计划。而由于Tesla决定向SolarCity提出要约，并且埃隆支持这一决定，因此即使尚未达成最终协议，修改他的附表13D以向市场提供最新信息也是适当的。

segments.textEn: It's obviously our hope to engage in a due diligence process with SolarCity and ultimately reach that agreement. And all that information that you would customarily see at that time, including the agreement itself, and detailed financial information about the combined companies would be provided then. But the result of this is that this is actually a more transparent process because you're essentially seeing behind the curtains more than you would ordinarily see in a transaction because you're actually getting additional information up front at the offer stage and getting an advanced look at the strategic business rationale for the deal.
segments.textZh: 显然，我们希望与SolarCity开展尽职调查流程，并最终达成那项协议。届时通常会看到的所有信息，包括协议本身以及有关合并后公司的详细财务信息，都会在那时提供。但这样做的结果是，这实际上是一个更加透明的流程，因为与通常在一项交易中能看到的情况相比，你们实质上看到了更多幕后信息，因为你们实际上在要约阶段就预先获得了额外信息，并提前了解了这项交易的战略业务理由。

segments.textEn: And so with that, I'll actually pass it over to Elon so that he can speak more about the strategic rationale for the deal and why we do think that combining the two companies makes sense here.
segments.textZh: 那么接下来，我把话交给埃隆，请他进一步谈谈这项交易的战略理由，以及为什么我们确实认为将两家公司合并在这里是合理的。

segments.textEn: Sure, I did touch on most of this yesterday, but I think what this call is mostly going to be about is getting into maybe some of the detailed questions that people have.
segments.textZh: 当然，我昨天确实谈到了其中大部分内容，但我认为这次电话会议主要可能是深入讨论大家提出的一些详细问题。

segments.textEn: The,
segments.textZh: 这个，

segments.textEn: as I said yesterday, there's kind of three parts to, and as I said at the actually powerwall presentation last year, so just as part of why I think this is really quite an obviously correct move, is that in order to solve sustainable energy question, we need sustainable energy production, which is going to come primarily in the form of solar, overwhelmingly in the form of solar in our view. Then combine that with stationary storage and electric vehicle and you have a complete solution to a sustainable energy future.
segments.textZh: 正如我昨天所说，这大致包含3个部分，而且正如我去年在实际上Powerwall发布会上所说的，所以我认为这确实显然是正确行动的部分原因，就是要解决可持续能源问题，我们需要可持续能源生产，而在我们看来，这将主要以太阳能的形式出现，绝大多数将以太阳能的形式出现。然后，将其与固定式储能和电动汽车结合起来，你就获得了迈向可持续能源未来的完整解决方案。

segments.textEn: Those are the three parts that are needed and, and those are the three things that I think Tesla should be providing.
segments.textZh: 这就是所需要的3个部分，而且，而且我认为这就是Tesla应该提供的3样东西。

segments.textEn: And it just became increasingly obvious that as we're developing the powerwall and new versions of the powerwall, as we integrate more of the inverter, electronics and intelligence in the powerwall, it really, you really need to take the solar panels and the solar system into account when doing that. Otherwise you duplicate a lot of hardware that doesn't work together as well. It's more expensive, the installation cost is substantially higher.
segments.textZh: 而且，随着我们开发Powerwall和新版本的Powerwall，随着我们把更多逆变器、电子设备和智能功能集成到Powerwall中，一点变得越来越明显，那就是在这样做时，确实，你确实需要把太阳能板和太阳能系统考虑进去。否则，你会重复配置大量无法很好协同工作的硬件。这样成本更高，安装成本也高出很多。

segments.textEn: You've got to put the installer power wall, install the solar panels. If you've got an electric car, you've got to install the wall connector. And at home charging system, there's potentially three visits. There's at least two visits. And then in terms of the sales process itself, when we're selling somebody the powerwall, very often, if not almost always, they're curious about solar and want to do the same thing. So then not being able to sell them Solar directly at SolarCity, sorry, Tesla through our stores, is pretty inefficient.
segments.textZh: 你得让安装人员安装Powerwall，安装太阳能板。如果你有电动汽车，你还得安装壁挂式连接器。再加上家庭充电系统，可能需要上门3次。至少也要上门2次。而且就销售流程本身而言，当我们向某人销售Powerwall时，他们往往，即使不是几乎总是，也会对太阳能感到好奇，并希望做同样的事。所以，无法在SolarCity——抱歉，是Tesla——通过我们的门店直接向他们销售太阳能产品，效率非常低。

segments.textEn: But as you look ahead to say Model 3 and a $35,000 car, well that same person at the same moment we could sell them roughly an equivalent amount value of solar panels and a powerwall, effectively doubling, almost doubling the sale at that time and then putting it all in at the same time.
segments.textZh: 但如果展望一下，比如Model 3和一辆35,000美元的汽车，那么在同一时刻，我们可以向同一个人销售价值大致相当的太阳能板和一台Powerwall，实际上让当时的销售额翻倍，几乎翻倍，然后同时完成所有安装。

segments.textEn: So I think the, the word synergy is bad, it's like almost sort of a dirty word. But I think it's, I think these synergies are really just common sense. Like obviously it's more efficient to do this as an integrated system at the sale and at the installation and in terms of just general maintenance and managing the customer relationship.
segments.textZh: 所以我认为，“协同效应”这个词不太好，它几乎有点像一个脏词。但我认为，我认为这些协同效应其实就是常识。比如显然，在销售和安装时将其作为一个集成系统来做效率更高，在一般维护以及管理客户关系方面也是如此。

segments.textEn: And yeah, I think that makes it kind of a pretty obvious thing to do. And it's quite difficult to create integrated product if you're forced to be at an arm's length and be two different companies.
segments.textZh: 而且，是的，我认为这使它成为一件相当显而易见应该做的事。如果你被迫保持一定距离，并且是两家不同的公司，就很难打造集成产品。

segments.textEn: So.
segments.textZh: 所以。

segments.textEn: If we give a special deal to SolarCity and SolarCity is not part of Tesla, then why are we doing that?
segments.textZh: 如果我们给予SolarCity特殊待遇，而SolarCity又不是Tesla的一部分，那么我们为什么要这么做？

segments.textEn: So we can do that if SolarCity is part of Tesla. We can't do it if a separate company.
segments.textZh: 所以，如果SolarCity是Tesla的一部分，我们就可以这么做。如果是独立的公司，我们就不能这么做。

segments.textEn: So it just makes things, the execution I think a lot easier and cleaner and more effective. So that's why I said yesterday, I think it's really kind of a no brainer if we didn't do this, it would make Tesla's execution harder and worse.
segments.textZh: 所以这只是让事情，让执行工作在我看来容易得多、更清晰、更有效。所以这就是为什么我昨天说，我认为这确实算是一件不假思索就该做的事；如果我们不这么做，就会让Tesla的执行工作变得更困难、更糟糕。

segments.textEn: And I think the tide of history very strongly supports will be a sustainable energy future, primarily solar and virtually entirely electric vehicles. And there'll be things that temporarily interrupt that type of industry but in the long term it will overwhelm everything. And our goal is to accelerate the advent of that future as fast as possible and this helps us accelerate it. So that's the reason.
segments.textZh: 而且我认为，历史潮流非常强有力地表明，未来将是一个可持续能源的未来，主要依靠太阳能，车辆也几乎将全部是电动汽车。会有一些事情暂时打断这类行业的发展，但从长远来看，它将压倒一切。我们的目标是尽可能快地加速那个未来的到来，而这会帮助我们加速实现它。所以，这就是原因。

segments.textEn: And yeah, so yeah, and I think there have been some questions about like does this sort of really increase our debt position or lever up the bank our balance sheet. It really doesn't, I think really encourage people to take a close look at SolarCity.
segments.textZh: 而且，是的，所以，是的，我想也有人提出过一些问题，比如，这是否真的会增加我们的债务状况，或者提高银行——我们资产负债表的杠杆率。实际上并不会，我确实非常鼓励大家仔细研究一下SolarCity。

segments.textEn: What really matters is the recourse debt. Obviously the non recourse debt is, is not what matters and the cash flows generating that solicitity will generate it covers what's required with the recourse debt. So they are headed to cash flow positive situation for the next three to six months at the outside.
segments.textZh: 真正重要的是追索权债务。显然，无追索权债务并不是、并不是重要的部分，而solicitity产生的现金流会产生它，足以覆盖追索权债务所需的金额。所以最迟在未来3到6个月内，他们将进入现金流为正的状态。

segments.textEn: And that's where the company's been steering itself, reducing their growth rate to some degree to achieve that cash flow positive position. But they're very clearly on their way to getting there in short order. So actually we expect it to be a net cash generator, not a user of cash, particularly when taking into Account the dramatic reduction in the cost of sales of source systems sold through our store. Through our stores.
segments.textZh: 这正是公司一直在引导自己前往的方向，在一定程度上降低增长率，以实现现金流为正的状态。但他们显然正在迅速接近这个目标。所以实际上，我们预计它将成为净现金创造者，而不是现金使用者，尤其是考虑到通过我们的门店销售的来源系统，其销售成本会大幅下降。通过我们的门店。

segments.textEn: The biggest factor in SolarCity's increasing cost per watt in Q1 was their sales cost. So as soon as you they quite a big increase in sales cost that'll go radically another direction with sales through Tesla.

segments.textZh: 谢谢。我想我只是想了解一下，您认为对 SolarCity 的这次押注在多大程度上是押注储能成本下降，也就是说，我们已经看到一些针对净计量法规的拟议修改。而且，而且如果这种情况继续下去，或者出现更多这种情况，这种商业模式能维持多久？是否需要看到储能成本下降，它才能奏效？您对此的信心是否就是推进这笔交易的原因？

segments.textEn: Yeah, the storage costs are going to drop really dramatically with each passing year. And I think the.
segments.textZh: 是的，储能成本将逐年大幅下降。而且我认为。

segments.textEn: Exclusion of certain situations, like Nevada, maybe Arizona, which we're working to mitigate, it'll be ahead of the net metering situation.
segments.textZh: 除某些情况外，比如内华达州，或许还有亚利桑那州，我们正在努力缓解这些情况，它会领先于净计量方面的局势。

segments.textEn: In New York, a reasonable deal has been arranged. And basically this gets ahead of the net metering situation, call it roughly the two to three year time frame.
segments.textZh: 在纽约，已经达成了一项合理的安排。而且基本上，这会抢在净计量局势之前，大致可以说是在2至3年的时间范围内。

segments.textEn: It's definitely important for long term. And although some utilities will exaggerate the impact of solar on the grid, ultimately the impact of solar on the grid beyond a certain localized percentage does have an impact and you do need to buffer the power.
segments.textZh: 这对长期而言无疑很重要。尽管一些公用事业公司会夸大太阳能对电网的影响，但归根结底，当太阳能在局部地区所占比例超过某个水平后，确实会对电网产生影响，你确实需要对电力进行缓冲。

segments.textEn: So they have a value argument. It's just exaggerated. So it's obviously very important for the long term and yeah, it's going to work together. What we're talking about here, solar power, stationary storage, electric cars, this is Earth's solution and we're going to try to make that happen as fast as possible. segments.textZh: 所以他们的论点有其道理。只是有所夸大。因此，这对长期而言显然非常重要，而且，是的，它们会协同运作。嗯，我的意思是，这正是世界所需要的。这是地球的终极解决方案。我们在这里谈论的太阳能、固定式储能、电动汽车，这就是地球的解决方案，而我们将努力尽快使其成为现实。SolarCity 和 Tesla 带来的根本益处，将根据我们在多大程度上加速了这一转型来衡量。

segments.textEn: So we're going to try to make it happen as fast as possible.
segments.textZh: 所以我们将努力尽快使其成为现实。

segments.textEn: And I think we'll have a meaningful impact on that time frame and then
segments.textZh: 而且我认为我们将对这一时间范围产生实质性影响，然后

segments.textEn: maybe just two real quick ones if the deal is consummated. Have you given any thought or plan to provide segmented balance sheet or cash flow just to provide a little bit more transparency on each line? And then on a Technical point, you will do that? Yeah.

segments.textZh: 我的意思是，我确实认为透明度是有价值的。所以。

segments.textEn: We will want to show that transparency as much as we can.
segments.textZh: 我们会希望尽可能展现这种透明度。

segments.textZh: 在某些情况下，问题会是，成本究竟应该分配到哪里？但我确实认为，如果它像一个人们无法弄清楚的黑箱，然后不得不以某种方式解析哪些部分分别是什么，那会很棒。

segments.textZh: 所以我们不希望因为人们不确定，而让股票出现信息折价。因此我认为，信息越清晰，人们就越能理解公司的价值。各个部分。它不可避免地会让一些人得出他们或许不该得出的结论，或者说那些结论还为时过早。但我确实相信透明度。

segments.textEn: I think we've debated this since the early days of the roadster. I mean, very early proto roadsters that we had would do vehicle to grid.
segments.textZh: 我想，从 Roadster 的早期阶段起，我们就一直在讨论这个问题。我的意思是，我们当时非常早期的 Roadster 原型车就可以实现车辆向电网供电。

segments.textEn: But you do get a lot of complications with that. If you backflow power through car into the wall, when is the car allowed to do that? When is it not?
segments.textZh: 但这样做确实会带来许多复杂问题。如果让电力通过汽车反向流入墙上的线路，汽车什么时候可以这样做？什么时候不可以？

segments.textEn: I mean, how much do you allow the car battery to be drawn down? segments.textZh: 我的意思是，你允许汽车电池的电量被消耗到什么程度？而且我认为，如果房子里的灯还亮着，人们却不能开车，因为否则房子里的所有电力都会中断，他们会非常不满。所以我认为，正确的解决方案是将其拆分为车辆、固定式电池和太阳能。

segments.textEn: And then some need to supplement that power at the grid level by having utility scale solar battery installations.
segments.textZh: 然后还需要通过公用事业规模的太阳能电池装置，在电网层面补充一部分电力。

segments.textEn: Because you don't always have enough surface area on a house or certainly for an apartment building, you don't have enough surface area. So you got to kind of ground mount the utility scale solar battery system and feed that to the grid.
segments.textZh: 因为住宅的表面积并不总是足够，而对公寓楼来说，表面积肯定不够。所以你得把公用事业规模的太阳能电池系统安装在地面上，再向电网供电。

segments.textEn: But if anyone that's seen my powerwall presentation, it's remarkable how little land you need to power the entire United States. It's crazy. Like a little corner of Texas or Utah, that's all the United States power.
segments.textZh: 但如果有人看过我的 Powerwall 演示，就会发现，为整个美国供电所需的土地少得惊人。太疯狂了。就像得克萨斯州或犹他州的一个小角落，那就足以供应整个美国的电力。

segments.textEn: And then there's like one pixel inside that box that I showed, which is the box of how much land area you need to power the United States. segments.textZh: 然后，我展示的那个方框里面大概有1个像素，那个方框表示为美国供电需要多大的土地面积。那就像是一个小方框，正如我所说，可以放进得克萨斯州狭长地带的一小块地方，或者犹他州的一个角落。而在那个方框里面有1个像素。那就是为整个美国提供支持所需电池组的大小，也就是所需表面积，1个像素。

segments.textEn: So anyway, we're going to try to build that as fast as we can the US but throughout the world.
segments.textZh: 所以不管怎样，我们会尽可能快地在美国建设它，也会在全世界建设。

segments.textZh: 谢谢。

segments.textZh: 顺便说一下，埃隆关于 Tesla 能源产品的演示视频可以在我们的网站上观看。埃隆，现在已经到半小时这个时间点了。队列中还有9位提问者，所以我交由你来
segments.speakerZh: 杰夫·埃文森（投资者关系）

segments.textEn: determine how far along you want to go.
segments.textZh: 决定你想继续多久。

segments.textZh: 我们当然要，嗯，尽量回答每个人的问题，而且就像我说的，我真的会鼓励大家从长远角度思考。这一切将走向何方？我认为，如果你从长远角度考虑，Tesla 与 SolarCity 的融合确实毫无疑问。真正的问题只是什么时机适合进行这种融合。而且，那个，你知道，这基本上关系到 SolarCity 的产品路线图和 Tesla 的产品路线图，其中显然有，你知道，非常重要、极为关键的产品信息，我真希望能告诉你们。

segments.textZh: 不能。

segments.textEn: The timing is, if anything we're, you know, maybe we should have done this sooner, but I certainly don't think we're doing it too early.
segments.textZh: 至于时机，如果真要说什么的话，我们，你知道，也许本该更早这样做，但我当然不认为我们做得太早了。

segments.textEn: And then what, what's the long term picture? Long term picture is a world with sustainable power generation, with stationary storage to buffer that power and then electric cars.
segments.textZh: 那么，长期图景是什么？长期图景是这样一个世界：拥有可持续的电力生产，以固定式储能来缓冲这些电力，然后还有电动汽车。

segments.textEn: And Tesla is going to be the leader in all three. So if you believe that that's the future we're headed towards, which everything points to that being true. segments.textZh: 而 Tesla 将在这3个领域都成为领导者。所以，如果你相信这就是我们正在迈向的未来，而一切都表明确实如此。实际上，谈到汽油车，我们将来回望汽油车，就会像现在回望蒸汽机一样。那就像是一个阶段，有点奇怪。

segments.textEn: And we're going to look back on fossil fuel power generation the same way. It was a weird phase.
segments.textZh: 我们也会以同样的方式回望化石燃料发电。那是一个奇怪的阶段。

segments.textEn: Now we want to get out of that weird phase as soon as we can. segments.textZh: 现在，我们希望尽快摆脱那个奇怪的阶段。而这一切都是为了加快我们摆脱历史上这个特殊时刻的速度，那时我们挖出某种寒武纪层位的化石，然后把它们烧掉。我想你会告诉你的孙辈，比如，是啊，你不会相信我们过去都做些什么。就像我们过去会挖出恐龙和古老植物液化后的遗骸，把它们放进汽车里燃烧，从而让汽车移动，发电厂也做同样的事。

segments.textEn: And like that sounds crazy.
segments.textZh: 而且，那听起来很疯狂。

segments.textEn: That's what it's going to be in the future, obviously. So we're trying to have the non weird future get here as fast as possible.
segments.textZh: 显然，未来人们就是会这样看待它。所以我们正努力让那个不奇怪的未来尽快到来。

segments.textEn: Yeah, I mean, the problem is that I think we just, we hit the, you know, it's like we don't have a good basis for doing some special deal with SolarCity because there's effectively a conflict of interest. Like, ironically, conflict of interest goes away for one company, but it doesn't go away for two separate companies.
segments.textZh: 是的，我的意思是，问题在于，我认为我们只是，我们遇到了那个，你知道，就像我们没有一个与 SolarCity 达成某种特殊交易的良好基础，因为实际上存在利益冲突。具有讽刺意味的是，对于一家公司，利益冲突会消失，但对于两家独立的公司，它不会消失。

segments.textEn: So, like, there's not really a good rationale for just offering a special deal and only working with one company that I also happen to own.
segments.textZh: 所以，怎么说呢，其实没有什么充分的理由去专门提供一项特殊交易，而且只与一家碰巧也是我拥有的公司合作。

segments.textEn: You know, just, it's. I don't think we have a good moral legal basis for behaving in a special way to SolarCity unless we're. It's actually one company.
segments.textZh: 你知道，就是，这个。我认为我们没有充分的道德和法律依据以特殊方式对待 SolarCity，除非我们是。它实际上是一家公司。

segments.textEn: Got it. And then one more, if I can, could you just rank some of the things that you talked about in the order you look at it as far as revenue synergies from cross selling, the technical synergies of being able to work with on both the manufacturer, the panel side as well as the battery side, and then maybe the third one bucket being cost synergies. And then if I forgot any out there, maybe list those as well in kind of the order that you're thinking of them.
segments.textZh: 明白了。然后如果可以的话，我还有一个问题，您能否把您谈到的一些事项排个序，说明您如何看待交叉销售带来的收入协同效应、能够同时在制造商、面板方面以及电池方面开展合作所带来的技术协同效应，然后第三类或许是成本协同效应。如果我还遗漏了什么，也请按照您考虑它们的大致顺序列出来。

segments.textEn: Thanks.
segments.textZh: 谢谢。

segments.textEn: Yeah, I mean, I think we'll have a more definitive answer for you once this process wraps up.
segments.textZh: 是的，我是说，我想等这个流程结束后，我们会给您一个更明确的答案。

segments.textEn: So, I mean, I regard what I'm saying here as anecdotal, but it's kind of the way I think about it from a gut standpoint is first and foremost, do we offer what allows us to offer the most compelling product to consumers and businesses.
segments.textZh: 所以，我是说，我认为我在这里说的只是经验之谈，但从直觉角度来说，我大致是这样考虑的：首要的是，我们是否提供了能让我们向消费者和企业提供最具吸引力产品的东西。

segments.textEn: And a seamlessly integrated product that all just works together that's better. Like, you don't want to have to have a heterogeneous systems integration problem.
segments.textZh: 以及一种无缝集成、一切都能协同运作、更加出色的产品。比如，你不会希望面对异构系统集成问题。

segments.textEn: That's basically where the interfaces break down and then people are sort of pointing fingers like, this didn't work, no yours thing didn't work. If it's just one integrated system, there's no finger pointing. You can iron out all the bugs and it just works.
segments.textZh: 基本上就是接口会在那里出问题，然后人们就会互相指责，比如，这个没起作用，不，是你的东西没起作用。如果只有一个集成系统，就不会有人互相指责。你可以解决所有缺陷，然后它就能正常运作。

segments.textEn: And you're not wondering, should I blame the solar company or the battery company or the. Who knows? It's just like sort of a pain in the butt to try to figure that out if you're the end customer.
segments.textZh: 而且你不会疑惑，我该怪太阳能公司，还是电池公司，或者那个。谁知道呢？如果你是终端客户，要设法弄清楚这一点简直就是件麻烦事。

segments.textEn: And I think we can guide the integrated product to be the right to just be right to be better.
segments.textZh: 而且我认为，我们可以引导集成产品，使其成为正确的产品，就是做到正确，做到更好。

segments.textEn: So that's kind of from that standpoint more than anything else.
segments.textZh: 所以，与其他任何事情相比，主要还是出于这个角度。

segments.textEn: And then in addition, there's just obvious cost savings to be had. If in the same store we can sell twice as much dollar volume, like, well, it's the same store not selling twice as much stuff.
segments.textZh: 除此之外，显然还能节省成本。如果我们能在同一家门店实现2倍的销售额，那么，嗯，还是同一家门店，并不是卖出2倍那么多的东西。

segments.textEn: And if with the installation crew, if they're now able to knock out three things in a single visit rather than schedule two or three separate visits, that's also way better.
segments.textZh: 而且就安装团队而言，如果他们现在一次上门就能完成3件事，而不必安排2次或3次单独上门，那也会好得多。

segments.textEn: You know, one can argue this sort of how much better is it? It's definitely some percentage better. That's material, which is kind of, I mean, that's kind of like the threshold for making a decision. It's obviously going to be a lot better. Like if you just cut the visits down to, you know, from two or three to one. Okay, you've probably cut your transport, labor and logistics cost maybe in half, something like that.
segments.textZh: 你知道，人们可以争论这到底能好多少？肯定会好某个百分比。这是重大的，也就是，我是说，这有点像作出决定的门槛。显然会好很多。比如，如果你直接把上门次数从，你知道，2次或3次减少到1次。好吧，你大概能把运输、人工和物流成本削减一半左右，差不多这样。

segments.textEn: And if you have a seamlessly integrated product, you can have less servicing costs and things are going to break down less.
segments.textZh: 而且如果你拥有无缝集成的产品，就可以降低服务成本，东西发生故障的次数也会减少。

segments.textEn: It's just the thing you'd want to buy. If you're the end customer, why would you want to buy anything else?
segments.textZh: 这就是你会想买的东西。如果你是终端客户，为什么还会想买其他任何东西？

segments.textEn: Now, Seva, apart from that, over the years, has this idea been bandied about with some of our largest shareholders, institutional shareholders? segments.textEn: We could do that and then potentially offer, just have the car there in a gallery format, something like that. So it does open up additional options on the retail front. Actually, now that you mentioned it,
segments.textZh: 我们可以那样做，然后可能提供，只是以展厅形式把车放在那里，诸如此类。所以这确实在零售方面带来了更多选择。其实，既然你提到了，

segments.textEn: I'm just wondering whether a car dealer association can say that it's a dealership, if it's selling more than cars, if it's also selling solar panels and power walls, and if it's going to change the look of the stores significantly enough that helps you guys out with that.
segments.textZh: 我只是想知道，如果一家门店销售的不只是汽车，还销售太阳能电池板和 Powerwall，而且门店的外观会发生足够显著的变化，从而在这方面帮助到你们，那么汽车经销商协会是否还能说它是一家经销店。

segments.textEn: Yeah, I think we'll still be prevented from actually including a car transaction even if it's part of a broader store.
segments.textZh: 是的，我认为，即使它是一家业务范围更广的门店，我们实际上仍会被禁止在其中进行汽车交易。

segments.textEn: But usually there's not a limit on having galleries where you simply display the car and have information about it.
segments.textZh: 但通常并不限制设立仅用于展示汽车并提供相关信息的展厅。

segments.textEn: And we could still conclude transactions for solar and batteries.
segments.textZh: 而且我们仍然可以完成太阳能和电池的交易。

segments.textEn: Yeah, so I mean, something like that. It does open up additional possibilities. Now that you mentioned it.
segments.textZh: 是的，所以我的意思是，类似那样。这确实带来了更多可能性。既然你提到了。

segments.textEn: Thanks.
segments.textZh: 谢谢。

segments.textEn: Thank you. Our next question comes from Station Shaw of Albert Freed. Your line is now open.
segments.textZh: 谢谢。我们的下一个问题来自 Albert Freed 的 Station Shaw。您的线路现已接通。

segments.textEn: Hi, I just have a follow up. So you mentioned the positives of rolling up SolarCity and you know, I think somebody earlier mentioned in so many words that, you know, the analysts have been saying that this is a bailout of SolarCity. So you know, can you just mention if shareholders don't vote for this, what happens? You mentioned that SolarCity in the next three to six months should be net cash generator. So it's not as bleak as some of these analysts have been saying.
segments.textZh: 你好，我只是想追问一下。所以你提到了整合 SolarCity 的积极面，而且你知道，我想之前有人用各种说法提到，你知道，分析师们一直说这是在救助 SolarCity。所以，你知道，能否请你说一下，如果股东不投票支持，会发生什么？你提到 SolarCity 在未来3到6个月内应该会成为净现金创造者。所以情况并不像其中一些分析师一直说的那么黯淡。

segments.textEn: SolarCity would be in a position if they don't vote for the potential transaction with Tesla. And then secondly, what does this, you know, what does this deal mean for your gigafactory? Does it have any change? Timeline has changed because you're going to have more of a capacity or not. Thank you. Sure.
segments.textZh: 如果他们不投票支持与 Tesla 的潜在交易，SolarCity 将处于一种境地。其次，这对你的超级工厂意味着什么，你知道，这笔交易对你的超级工厂意味着什么？会有什么变化吗？时间表已经改变，因为你们会有更多产能，还是没有。谢谢。好的。

segments.textEn: I don't know where this bailout stuff comes from because I mean, Tesla's not the one deciding what the market value of Sol City is. It's, you know, the stock market is. So Seoul City could certainly raise capital equity on its current valuation without any problem.
segments.textZh: 我不知道这种救助的说法从何而来，因为，我是说，并不是 Tesla 在决定 Sol City 的市场价值。是，你知道，是股市在决定。所以 Seoul City 完全可以按照其当前估值筹集股权资本，不会有任何问题。

segments.textEn: So. And Solid City is headed to like a very, very healthy place from a cash flow standpoint in short order. So, you know, next three to five months getting to cash flow positive. So if a company's around the corner from being cash flow positive and has the ability to raise equity capital on its own, I don't see how an acquisition is in any way bailout. That's obviously a false description.
segments.textZh: 所以。而且从现金流角度来看，Solid City 很快就会迈向一个非常、非常健康的状态。所以，你知道，未来3到5个月就会实现正现金流。所以，如果一家公司即将实现正现金流，并且有能力自行筹集股权资本，我看不出收购怎么会以任何方式算是救助。这显然是一种错误的描述。

segments.textEn: And then the gigafactory kind of proceeds independently of SolarCity. Except that obviously we would gear the product, the storage product would be geared towards a SolarCity type system.
segments.textZh: 然后，超级工厂基本上独立于 SolarCity 推进。只不过显然我们会调整产品，储能产品会面向 SolarCity 类型的系统进行调整。

segments.textEn: And this wouldn't be something that would be explicitly exclusionary to other solar companies, by the way. It would just be that other solar companies would have to match the SolarCity product in order to use our battery product most effectively. So it's not about sort of trying to shut up other solar companies. It's just about being able to guide the product to where it needs to go and then, you know, we'll do the right thing with other solar companies if they're also guiding their products to match.
segments.textZh: 顺便说一下，这并不意味着会明确排斥其他太阳能公司。只是其他太阳能公司必须与 SolarCity 的产品相匹配，才能最有效地使用我们的电池产品。所以这并不是要设法让其他太阳能公司闭嘴。只是为了能够引导产品走向它需要去的方向，然后，你知道，如果其他太阳能公司也在引导其产品实现匹配，我们也会正确对待它们。

segments.textEn: So we're not going to basically be a jerk to other solar companies.
segments.textZh: 所以我们基本上不会对其他太阳能公司表现得像个混蛋。

segments.textEn: This is really about being laser focused on having the most compelling consumer solution.
segments.textZh: 这实际上是要高度专注于提供最具吸引力的消费者解决方案。

segments.textEn: Yeah, that's I think the right thing to do.
segments.textZh: 是的，我认为那是正确的做法。

segments.textEn: Okay, thank you very much. Congratulations, Gan.
segments.textZh: 好的，非常感谢。恭喜，Gan。

segments.textEn: Thanks.
segments.textZh: 谢谢。

segments.textEn: Thank you. And our next question comes from Hank Elder of Goldman Sachs. The line is now open.
segments.textZh: 谢谢。我们的下一个问题来自高盛的 Hank Elder。线路现已接通。

segments.textEn: Hey guys, this is actually Brian Lee on for Hank. I have just three housekeeping questions more along the deal itself and, and in the interest of time, I'll just run through these quickly. First is, given SolarCity's relationships with various lenders and tax equity fund structures, I was hoping you could talk to any visibility into potential change in control provisions and or exposure to clawback provisions on solar tax credits that might exist.
segments.textZh: 嘿，各位，其实我是代 Hank 提问的 Brian Lee。我只有3个事务性问题，更多是关于交易本身的，而且为了节省时间，我会快速把这些问题过一遍。第一个是，鉴于 SolarCity 与各类贷款方以及税务股权基金结构之间的关系，我希望你们能谈谈，是否能看清可能存在的控制权变更条款，以及／或者太阳能税收抵免追回条款方面的风险敞口。

segments.textEn: Second question would be as part of the due diligence, will the board consider other alternatives to SolarCity? And that, and then third one, and I'll pass it on, is are there any collars or caps on the stock exchange ratio being proposed? And if not, what's the rationale for that?
segments.textZh: 第二个问题是，作为尽职调查的一部分，董事会会考虑 SolarCity 之外的其他选择吗？然后，第三个问题，问完我就交给下一位，拟议的股票交换比率是否设有任何上下限？如果没有，其理由是什么？

segments.textEn: As to the beginning, really this is kind of the beginning of the analysis, not the end. And normally it would be a lot closer to the end because large shelter in both companies, it's, you know, it's something we have to talk about at the beginning where we don't have all the answers, but then we will compile those and present those to shareholders for their decision in the months to come.
segments.textZh: 关于一开始，实际上这算是分析的开端，而不是终点。通常它会更接近终点，因为两家公司都有大型避税安排，这，你知道，是我们必须在一开始就讨论的事情，而这时我们还没有所有答案，但随后我们会汇总这些答案，并在未来几个月提交给股东，由他们作出决定。

segments.textEn: So obviously part of that diligence process would be talking to the lenders, making sure they're comfortable. I think it's a good idea. Pretty sure they will, but we got to talk to them and yeah, and then in terms of other companies, we did consider that and it's part of the initial diligence process. But we think SolarCity is the best company out there.
segments.textZh: 所以，显然该尽职调查流程的一部分会是与贷款方交谈，确保他们对此感到放心。我认为这是个好主意。相当确定他们会放心，但我们得和他们谈谈，没错，然后就其他公司而言，我们确实考虑过，而这是初步尽职调查流程的一部分。但我们认为 SolarCity 是目前最好的公司。

segments.textEn: And it's good, but it's sort of a leader in the field.
segments.textZh: 而且它很好，不过它算是该领域的领导者。

segments.textEn: It has this labo technology.
segments.textZh: 它拥有这种拉博技术。

segments.textEn: The product direction, we believe, is correct in terms of making rapid progress towards a highly differentiated product.
segments.textZh: 我们认为，在朝着高度差异化产品快速推进方面，这一产品方向是正确的。

segments.textEn: There's no other company out there that's like that at all.
segments.textZh: 目前完全没有其他公司是这样的。

segments.textEn: Thank you. And our next question comes from Trip Chari of Global Equities Research. Your line is now open.
segments.textZh: 谢谢。我们的下一个问题来自 Global Equities Research 的 Trip Chari。您的线路现已接通。

segments.textEn: Thank you. I have a quick question for Ilan. I was just wondering, like, how does
segments.textZh: 谢谢。我有一个简短的问题想问伊兰。我只是想知道，比如，怎么会

segments.textEn: this acquisition plays out with the opportunities that Tesla may find in micro grids and grid space?
segments.textZh: 收购将如何影响 Tesla 可能在微电网和电网领域发现的机会？

segments.textEn: Yeah, I mean, we want to have.
segments.textZh: 是的，我是说，我们想要拥有。

segments.textEn: I think it's always good to like, productize things. So it's kind of like you can click here and buy your micro grid.
segments.textZh: 我认为把东西产品化总是好的。所以这有点像，你可以点击这里，购买你的微电网。

segments.textEn: Versus having a tailored situation all over the place. If you can productize can just happen real fast. And so I think like productizing microgrid, just click here and you get a microgrid. It just works. That's. I think that's a good way to go.
segments.textZh: 而不是到处都有定制化的情形。如果你能产品化，就能非常快地实现。因此我认为，比如把微电网产品化，只需点击这里，你就能获得一个微电网。它就是能用。那是。我认为那是个不错的方向。

segments.textEn: You know, I think consumers obviously appreciate things that are easy, simple, fast.
segments.textZh: 你知道，我认为消费者显然喜欢容易、简单、快速的东西。

segments.textEn: But actually corporate customers, utilities, they appreciate that too, because they don't have to go through this big, laborious process. And it's a pain in the butt for them. It blows their mind when they can just sort of click a button and then we installed their thing and it works.
segments.textZh: 但实际上，企业客户、公用事业公司也很欣赏这一点，因为他们不必经历这个庞大而费力的流程。这对他们来说很麻烦。当他们只需点一下按钮，然后我们就为他们安装好设备，而且它能正常运行时，他们都惊呆了。

segments.textEn: Just because the product's big doesn't mean that the whole process needs to be complex. Bigness and complexity are not the same thing.
segments.textZh: 产品体积大，并不意味着整个流程就需要很复杂。体积大和复杂不是一回事。

segments.textEn: So I think some of our utility customers have been quite pleasantly surprised by just how easy it is to implement, and it's going to get a lot easier in the future.
segments.textZh: 所以我认为，我们的一些公用事业客户对实施起来竟然如此容易感到相当惊喜，而且未来还会容易得多。

segments.textEn: All right, I think that's the end of the questions. Thank you, Todd, Elon and the rest of the team. Thank you, Terea, and thank you, investors, for all the interest. If you have any closing remarks. Elon, otherwise we can end it there.
segments.textZh: 好的，我想问题就到这里。谢谢Todd、埃隆以及团队的其他成员。谢谢你，Terea，也感谢各位投资者的关注。埃隆，如果你有什么结束语，可以说一下；否则我们就到此结束。
segments.speakerZh: 杰夫·埃文森（投资者关系）

segments.textEn: No, I think those are a lot of great questions. And then obviously we'll have a lot more information as the diligence process concludes, hopefully reasonably near future.
segments.textZh: 没有，我认为这些都是非常好的问题。显然，随着尽职调查流程结束，我们会有更多信息，希望是在相当近的将来。

segments.textEn: But I think it's easy to get sort of mired in the details. But if I think the right thing is to sort of look up into the future and say, where is this headed? What are the macro trends?
segments.textZh: 但我认为，人们很容易有点陷在细节里。但如果我认为正确的做法是稍微抬起头来展望未来，并问：这将走向何方？宏观趋势是什么？

segments.textEn: Does this action match where the tides of history are going? And that's really what's going to make the difference in the long term.
segments.textZh: 这一行动是否符合历史潮流的方向？而这才是真正会在长期产生影响的因素。

segments.textEn: So I just encourage people to think in that way.
segments.textZh: 所以我只是鼓励人们以这种方式思考。

segments.textEn: All right, thank you.
segments.textZh: 好的，谢谢。
segments.speakerZh: 杰夫·埃文森（投资者关系）

segments.textEn: Everybody, have a great day.
segments.textZh: 祝大家今天愉快。

segments.textEn: Ladies and gentlemen, thank you for your participation on today's conference. This concludes your program. You may now disconnect. Everyone, have a great day.
segments.textZh: 女士们、先生们，感谢各位参加今天的电话会议。本次会议到此结束。现在可以断开连接。祝大家今天愉快。

segments.textEn: Sa.
segments.textZh: 萨。
